resource.name: Annual Mean Concentration of Haloacetic Acids (HAA5) in Drinking Water, 2022
resource.description: This dataset describes the annual mean concentration of the contaminant, haloacetic acids (HAA5), in community water systems across Tennessee in 2022.
resource.attribution: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC)
columns_description: County FIPS code assigned by the U.S. Census Bureau to identify counties
Number assigned to line of data for identification purposes
Year of analysis
Name of county
Average concentration level of analyte observed in county's drinking water, measured in micrograms per liter (ug/L)
Maximum contaminant level category (1=Greater than MCL, 2=Less than or equal to MCL, 3=Not detected)
Number of people drinking water is supplied to, in a county
Identification number assigned to public water system (PWS)

domain_metadata.value: The maximum contaminant level (MCL) for haloacetic acids, according to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), is 60ug/L (0.060 mg/L). Data represented shows the yearly average concentration of the potential contaminant.
Division of Communicable and Environmental Diseases and Emergency Preparedness (CEDEP)

The disinfection byproducts (DBP) covered by these data include Haloacetic acids (HAA). The regulated Haloacetic acids, known as HAA5, are: Monochloroacetic acid, Dichloroacetic acid, Trichloroacetic acid, Monobromoacetic acid, and Dibromoacetic acid.
Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC)

Blank or missing values in the 'PWS ID" variable indicates that geographic information did not produce reliable and accurate boundaries and thus cannot be provided within the dataset. To locate a community water system of interest within your county, please use EPA's Community Water System Service Area Boundaries map (https://www.epa.gov/ground-water-and-drinking-water/community-water-system-service-area-boundaries?tab=map)
